newsitem.title: UK: Mideast/Asia crude tanker rates edge higher again.
newsitem.headline: Mideast/Asia crude tanker rates edge higher again.

text.p: Rates for crude oil tankers plying Mideast/Asia routes edged higher again on Friday in thin business and shipbrokers attributed the gains to a relative scarcity of tonnage.

Brokers assessed Mideast/Japan Rates at W50 or slightly below and said the fresh fixtures of the 260,000 tonne Mountain Cloud to Singapore at W49, and the 250,000 tonne Astro Alpha to Thailand at W52.5, as being roughly on the market.
"It has perked up a little bit," one London-based broker said. "There was a lot of fixing last week and a lot of the tonnage is now gone," he said.
But he added that London-based activity had been hard hit by post-election torpor.
Brokers Galbraiths said in a weekly report: "The market still looks set for a further rise in freight rates, particularly on modern ships to the Arabian Gulf."

Business from West Africa to the U.S. was also looking perky although Valero's fixture of the 130,000 tonne London Splendour to the U.S. Gulf at W100 was seen 2.5 to five points above market levels. "Chartering has picked up a bit," one broker said, however.

Inter/UKCont rates for 130,000 tonne Suezmaxes were pegged little changed at around W92.5/W95, although Aframaxes were seen oversupplied in the North Sea - 16 spot ships are currently waiting for cargoes, according to Galbraith's.
"Even if business picks up dramatically in the next few days rates will remain low with W90 looking to be about the maximum anyone can expect."
